title: Python SDK policy rule helpers: policy types, write lock, condition tuples and rule builders

prose.text: These are claims about the Python SDK's policy rule helpers. Rule ordering semantics are in [[zpa.terraform.rule-order]], and the wire shapes are in [[zpa.api.policy-wire]].

checks.do: Whether a rule's conditions all reached the request: the v1 builder keeps only three-element tuples and dictionaries.
Whether a v1 App Protection rule add was serialized with the other rule writes; it is not.
Whether the policy type name is a key of POLICY_MAP, not the API enum name.
Whether a rule write for portal or user portal policy was expected from the generic delete and reorder calls.
Whether several processes or hosts write policy rules at the same time, since the lock does not cover them.
Whether concurrent threads in one process call delete or reorder, which take the same lock as add and update.

rule-lock-gaps.statement: The v1 `add_app_protection_rule` has no lock decorator, although the other add and update helpers do.

v1-conditions-forms.statement: The v1 condition builder accepts a tuple of three elements (object type, lhs, rhs), optionally wrapped as ("AND" or "OR", tuple), and a dictionary with id, negated, operator and operands; operands of the same object type are grouped into one block with that type's operator, defaulting to OR.

operator = condition[0].upper() condition = condition[1]  # The second element is the actual condition

v1-conditions-dropped.statement: A v1 condition that is neither a three-element tuple nor a dictionary is skipped without an error: for example the two-element form ("client_type", [...]) used by the v2 builder, or a condition given as a list, as conditions loaded from JSON are, whether a three-element list or one wrapped with "AND" or "OR".
v1-conditions-dropped.conditions: The skip follows from the builder having no else branch after the tuple and dictionary cases, and from both the operator unwrap and the three-element case testing for a tuple; it was not run. The list case was added because the v1.11.1 changelog says conditions now accept lists while the v1 builder still does not (divergence v1-list-conditions); previously "A v1 condition that is neither a three-element tuple nor a dictionary, for example the two-element form (\"client_type\", [...]) used by the v2 builder, is skipped without an error."

v2-conditions-forms.statement: The v2 condition builder reads a tuple as the object type (lower-cased) followed by its values; since v1.11.1 it reads a list the same way, where up to v1.10.0 it accepted only tuples and a list-shaped condition was dropped (#583). It puts app and app_group values in one block, puts console, location, machine_grp, client_type and user_portal each in their own block with the operator, and turns posture, trusted_network, country_code, platform, risk_factor_type, saml, scim and scim_group lists of (lhs, rhs) pairs into entryValues.
v2-conditions-forms.conditions: Changed upstream in v1.11.1 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "The v2 condition builder reads a tuple as the object type (lower-cased) followed by its values; it puts app and app_group values in one block, puts console, location, machine_grp, client_type and user_portal each in their own block with the operator, and turns posture, trusted_network, country_code, platform, risk_factor_type, saml, scim and scim_group lists of (lhs, rhs) pairs into entryValues." The v1 builder still checks for tuples only.

access-rule-v1-uses-v1.statement: `add_access_rule` builds its conditions with the v1 builder.

get-rule-two-calls.statement: `get_rule` first calls `get_policy` for the policy type to find the policy set ID and then requests the rule under that policy set, so one lookup is two requests.

python-v2-operand-forms.statement: The Python SDK's v2 condition builder emits `entryValues` (pairs of `lhs` and `rhs`) for the object types posture, trusted_network, country_code, platform, risk_factor_type, saml, scim, scim_group and chrome_enterprise, and a `values` list for every other type. Its v1 builder emits flat `{objectType, lhs, rhs}` operands.

python-v2-operand-forms.conditions: The MCP-side statement of the same split is in zpa.policy.conditions. chrome_enterprise was added because its builder branch also emits entryValues; previously "...for the object types posture, trusted_network, country_code, platform, risk_factor_type, saml, scim and scim_group, and a `values` list for every other type."

python-credential-exclusive.statement: The Python credential rule builder first fetches the credential policy set with a GET through `get_policy`; then, before sending the rule, it refuses when both or neither of `credential_id` and `credential_pool_id` are given, returning the message as a string in the error slot rather than raising. It sends the id as `credential` or as `credentialPool`.
python-credential-exclusive.conditions: Corrected because the get_policy request runs before the check and the refusal is a returned string; previously "The Python credential rule builder refuses, before any request, to proceed when both or neither of `credential_id` and `credential_pool_id` are given; it sends the id as `credential` or as `credentialPool`."

The Go SDK's `CreateRule` and `UpdateRule`, in both policy packages, add no condition.

python-isolation-client-type.conditions: Extended per verifier to add_browser_protection_rule_v2 and update_browser_protection_rule_v2, which append the same condition (v1.10.0 and HEAD). Applies to the add and update isolation builders; the Go-side absence is a read of the two Go policy packages (no client-type string appears in CreateRule or UpdateRule).

python-capabilities-mapping.statement: The Python capability rule builder turns its flags into the strings CLIPBOARD_COPY, CLIPBOARD_PASTE, FILE_DOWNLOAD, FILE_UPLOAD, INSPECT_FILE_UPLOAD, INSPECT_FILE_DOWNLOAD, MONITOR_SESSION, RECORD_SESSION and SHARE_SESSION, and maps `file_upload=False` to INSPECT_FILE_UPLOAD (not to nothing), while `file_upload=True` gives FILE_UPLOAD. The OpenAPI document types `capabilities` as a free list of strings, and the Go SDK tests exercise five of the values.
python-capabilities-mapping.conditions: Which capability strings the API accepts is not enumerated in the OpenAPI document.

python-redirection-rules.statement: The Python redirection rule builder rejects `redirect_default` when `service_edge_group_ids` is given, requires `service_edge_group_ids` for `redirect_preferred` and `redirect_always`, checks the first value of each `CLIENT_TYPE` operand, and only the first, against five client types, and rejects the branch and edge connector client types when the action is `redirect_always`. The OpenAPI document lists REDIRECT_DEFAULT, REDIRECT_PREFERRED and REDIRECT_ALWAYS as actions.

python-redirection-rules.conditions: These are client-side checks in the Python SDK; the Go SDK has none. Whether the API enforces the same rules is not shown. The client-type clause was narrowed because the check reads only operand["values"][0]; previously it said the builder "limits `CLIENT_TYPE` values to five client types".

python-timeout-defaults.statement: The Python `add_timeout_rule_v2` and `update_timeout_rule_v2` send `reauthTimeout` 172800 and `reauthIdleTimeout` 600 when the caller does not pass them, so an update that omits them writes those values rather than leaving the rule's current ones.

python-timeout-defaults.conditions: Whether the API treats the values as seconds is not stated in the pinned spec; the type difference with the Go SDK is divergence zpa.policy.timeout-rules reauth-value-type.

python-bulk-reorder-passthrough.conditions: That the function never references Default_Rule is a negative read of the pinned file (a grep for Default_Rule in policies.py finds nothing); the quoted body from the method to its return covers every statement after the docstring.

generic-calls-use-map.statement: `get_policy` and `list_rules` look the type up in `POLICY_MAP` without further filtering, and `delete_rule` resolves its policy set through `get_policy(policy_type, ...)`.

fixed-type-writes.statement: The add and update rule methods named for a policy type resolve their policy set with a fixed type, for example `add_access_rule` with `get_policy("access", ...)`.

lock-object.statement: `policies.py` defines one module-level `Lock()` named `global_rule_lock`, and a `synchronized` decorator that runs a function inside `with lock:`.

lock-add-update.statement: The decorator is applied to the v1 and v2 add and update rule methods, for example `add_access_rule`, `update_access_rule_v2` and `add_browser_protection_rule_v2`.

lock-delete-reorder.statement: The same decorator is applied to `delete_rule`, `reorder_rule` and `bulk_reorder_rules`.

lock-process-local.statement: The lock serializes threads of one Python process only.
lock-process-local.conditions: Follows from the lock being a threading.Lock held in module memory. Another process, host or tool writing rules at the same time is not covered.

portal-rule-writes.title: Whether rule add and update work for the portal and user portal policy types
portal-rule-writes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: add_rule, update_rule and delete_rule also work for PRIVILEGED_PORTAL_POLICY and USER_PORTAL; the SDK has no generic add or update that takes a policy type name, and no source shows the service accepting those writes.
portal-rule-writes.blocks: writing portal or user portal policy rules through the Python SDK

v1-list-conditions.summary: The v1.11.1 changelog says ZPA policy conditions now accept lists, but the v1 condition builder still accepts only tuples and dictionaries.

positions.says: The changelog says policy conditions now accept lists as well as tuples, and that list-shaped conditions were previously dropped.

quotes: ZPA policy `conditions` now accept lists as well as tuples (e.g. conditions loaded from JSON); list-shaped conditions were previously dropped.

positions.says: `_create_conditions_v1` still tests for a three-element tuple or a dictionary, so a list-shaped condition is still dropped there; only the v2 builder accepts lists.

v1-list-conditions.impact: A rule written through a v1 helper (add_access_rule, add_timeout_rule, add_client_forwarding_rule, add_isolation_rule, add_app_protection_rule or their update methods) with conditions loaded from JSON is sent without those conditions, and no error is returned. Convert each condition to a tuple, or use the v2 helpers.
